subject: Private deployment: consolidated outbound connectivity & firewall requirements
messages:
From: Anita Shah <anita.shah@bluepeakhealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: BluePeak IT Security <it-security@bluepeakhealth.com>
Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Private deploy: outbound connectivity requirements for Redwood Private

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for taking the call earlier. We're kicking off the networking review for the Redwood Private deployment (VPC-connected, customer-managed NAT/proxy) and need a single, authoritative list of what to allow from our perimeter to ensure the control plane and runtime function without surprises. Specifically we need:

- Minimum set of FQDNs and IP ranges to whitelabel on our egress NAT/proxy
- Ports and protocols (we assume 443, any other TCP/UDP?)
- Whether DNS lookups need to be resolved through our proxy or allowed to reach public resolvers
- TLS expectations: do you require end-to-end TLS (yes) and do you block TLS inspection / active MITM? Any certificate pinning?
- mTLS requirements for control plane / metrics endpoints (yes/no)
- Any webhook/callback endpoints (for alerts/telemetry) and their expected origins
- Recommended pattern: static NAT IPs vs outbound proxy with CONNECT (and what breaks if we do TLS interception)

We also need an estimated IP rotation schedule if you publish IP ranges that may change. Can you send this back as a short, prescriptive checklist we can hand to our networking team?

Target for internal signoff here is Jan 20 — if you can get something by next week that’d be great.

Thanks,
Anita Shah
Director, IT Operations
BluePeak Health

Subject: Re: Private deploy: outbound connectivity requirements for Redwood Private

Hi Anita — thanks for the clear list. I pulled together an initial, prescriptive set of requirements and attached a one-page summary (egress-endpoints-v1.pdf). High level: we keep outbound to a minimal set of hostnames and recommend static NAT IPs for control plane traffic where possible. A few quick notes up front:

- Primary outbound destinations (FQDNs): control.redwood.ai, telemetry.redwood.ai, updates.redwood.ai, pkg.redwood.ai
- Protocols/ports: outbound TCP 443 only (all service endpoints listen on 443). We do not require any non-443 ports for normal operation.
- DNS: allow DNS resolution to public resolvers or internal resolvers that forward to public. We rely on name resolution for the endpoint hostnames.
- TLS: TLS 1.2+ required. We do NOT require mTLS for customer-to-control-plane (control plane authenticates using tokens). However some internal telemetry endpoints will accept mTLS if you prefer that extra lock. TLS inspection is supported but not recommended for control-plane traffic because client certificate validation and SNI-based routing are used by our runtime; if you must enable interception, please ensure SNI is preserved and that interception does not break OCSP/CRL checking.
- Webhooks/callbacks: outbound alerting may call back to your configured endpoint only if you register it; otherwise no inbound callbacks are initiated to arbitrary hosts.
- Networking pattern: static NAT IPs are preferred for predictable firewalling; outbound proxy with CONNECT works but you must allow TLS passthrough (no header rewrite) and permit CONNECT to the above FQDNs.

I'm looping in Laura and Jonas to confirm the exact IP ranges and rotation cadence. I'll follow up once we finalize the RFC.

Best,
Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Jonas/Laura — forwarding Anita's request and the draft response I sent below. Need your infra/ops confirmation on the concrete IP ranges we can publish and the expected rotation policy. Key decision points for the template:

1) IP publishing strategy
   - Option A (preferred): publish a small set of static egress IPs per-region (e.g., 3 per region) and only rotate on major infra changes. Customers can safely whitelist those IPs at the perimeter.
   - Option B: recommend customers whitelist FQDNs and allow DNS-resolved egress, with an optional proxy. This is more brittle for strict firewalls.

2) TLS inspection compatibility
   - Our runtime uses SNI and token headers for routing. TLS interception that strips SNI or rewrites headers will break request routing. We can document the exact headers but recommending 'TLS passthrough' is simpler.

3) Telemetry and metrics endpoints
   - telemetry.redwood.ai (443) for metrics/usage events. Host will accept both token-based TLS and optional mTLS for customers who require it. Recommend you advise customers that telemetry traffic is low-volume but near-real-time.

4) Health and control endpoints
   - control.redwood.ai (443) for agent heartbeats and control-plane commands. Needs to be reachable from runtime, low-latency.

5) Rotation cadence and notification
   - If we publish static IPs we should commit to a 90-day notice for any change, publish on the Customer Portal + HubSpot, and include a signed list with checksum.

Action items: Jonas, can you produce the conservative IP-range set (CIDR or /32s) we can publish for us-west-2 and us-east-1 by EOD Friday? Laura, please review the wording on TLS interception and confirm if we should offer an optional mTLS mode for control plane (I think telemetry only). I've attached the checklist template I usually use.

Thanks,
Rishi

Hi Anita — quick follow-up with the consolidated requirements and next steps (see bullets below). Jonas provided the conservative per-region IP list we recommend for whitelisting; we also included recommended FQDNs for people who prefer DNS-based allowances. The attached checklist is a one-page handoff for your networking team.

Consolidated, prescriptive requirements (customer-ready):

- Whitelist the following FQDNs (outbound TCP 443): control.redwood.ai, telemetry.redwood.ai, updates.redwood.ai, pkg.redwood.ai
- If you prefer IP-based whitelisting, allow the following static egress IPs (per-region):
  - us-west-2: 52.34.128.9, 52.34.128.10, 52.34.128.11
  - us-east-1: 34.210.45.21, 34.210.45.22, 34.210.45.23
- Ports/protocols: outbound TCP 443 only. No UDP or other TCP ports required for control plane or model serving.
- DNS: allow DNS resolution to public resolvers or your internal resolvers that forward externally. We resolve hostnames dynamically.
- TLS and interception: TLS 1.2+ required. TLS interception/passthrough is supported but must preserve SNI and OCSP/CRL behavior. If you perform active MITM, please test connectivity to control.redwood.ai and telemetry.redwood.ai before cutover — note that token-based auth relies on unmodified headers.
- mTLS: optional for telemetry endpoints; not required for control-plane tokens. If you request mTLS we will provide cert details and rotation guidance.
- Webhooks/callbacks: not required by default; we will only POST to endpoints you explicitly register.
- IP rotation/notice: static IPs are expected to be stable; we commit to 90-day advance notice for any changes to published egress IPs and a bulletin on the Customer Portal + HubSpot record.

Next steps:
- Please confirm if your team prefers IP whitelist or DNS/FQDN whitelist.
- If IP: share the contact and process for submitting a signed IP list acceptance.
- If using a proxy: confirm CONNECT behavior and whether your proxy will preserve SNI.

Attachments: egress-endpoints-v1.pdf (summary), redwood-private-egress-checklist.xlsx (handoff)

If you want, we can set up a 30-minute call with Jonas to walk the network team through the checklist and run a quick connectivity test.

Thanks — Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
